data.title: Walmart Stock (WMT) Target Slashed to $130 by Goldman Sachs as Sales Growth Slows
data.description:
Shares of Walmart Inc. (WMT), a U.S. retail company, had their price target cut by Wall Street bank Goldman Sachs (GS) to $130 on Thursday, August 20. The stock also fell over 9% at close after Walmart reported its fiscal 2026 second-quarter results, as investors focused on slower comparable-sales growth despite an earnings beat and higher 2026 guidance.

Goldman Sachs Lowers Walmart Stock Price Target

Goldman Sachs analyst Kate McShane lowered WMT's price target to $130 from $141 while maintaining a Buy rating. McShane said Walmart's valuation remains "stretched," even after the stock's recent decline.

However, the analyst remains positive about Walmart's second-half outlook. McShane cited the retailer's price investments, marketplace growth, and improving eCommerce profits as reasons for her optimism. She expects these factors to support further market-share gains through the rest of 2026.

Despite the positive outlook, McShane has lowered her 2026 earnings-per-share (EPS) estimate for Walmart by about 2%. Notably, Walmart's U.S. eCommerce business posted double-digit profit margins in the first half of the year, showing that the unit is becoming more profitable.

Walmart Stock Plummets 9% Despite Earnings Beat

Walmart shares fell over 9% at Thursday's close, significantly underperforming the S&P 500's (SPY) 0.9% decline. The stock extended those losses by about 0.41% in premarket trading on Friday, signaling more volatility, according to TipRanks data.

data.title: Stock Market News Today, 8/21/26 – Futures Rise Despite Higher Treasury Yields
data.description:
U.S. stock futures climbed ahead of Friday's session despite elevated Treasury yields, as investors assessed the government's plan to buy back long-dated Treasuries. Meanwhile, Thursday's sharp selloff put the major U.S. indexes on track for weekly losses.

Futures on the Nasdaq 100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 0.46%, 0.30%, and 0.39%, respectively, at 5:29 a.m. EDT on August 21.

Oil prices retreated from Thursday's rally but remained on track for a second consecutive weekly gain as the stalled U.S.-Iran conflict continued to disrupt supplies from the key Middle East oil-producing region.

At the time of writing, Brent crude (CM:BZ) traded around $93.03 a barrel, while WTI crude (CM:CL) was near $86.07 a barrel.

Major U.S. stock indices fell on Thursday, giving back the previous day's gains. Walmart's (WMT) post-earnings decline added pressure to the market, with the Dow, Nasdaq, and S&P 500 falling 1.32%, 1.00%, and 0.87%, respectively. The declines put the S&P 500 and Nasdaq down 1.9% and 2.5% for the week, while the Dow was down 1.8%.

The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield traded near 4.69% as of the last check. Additionally, the spot gold price in U.S. dollars traded around $4,587.26 per ounce on Friday.

No major earnings reports are scheduled for Friday.

Looking ahead, investors will watch reports on the S&P Global Manufacturing and Services PMI (Purchasing Managers' Index) later today.

European markets traded mostly lower as investors weighed concerns about rising yields.

Asia-Pacific Markets End Mixed

Asia-Pacific markets ended mixed, tracking losses on Wall Street in the previous session as bond yields remained elevated.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index gained 1.21%. In China, the Shanghai Composite rose 0.04%, while the Shenzhen Component was down 0.87%. In Japan, the Nikkei dropped 0.30%, and the Topix gained 0.19%.

BMO Sees D-Wave as a Quantum Computing Leader

Kumar believes D-Wave has an advantage because it already generates commercial revenue. He also pointed to its work across both annealing and gate-model quantum computing.

"We believe D-Wave is best positioned in the quantum space to have commercial success," Kumar said. He cited the company's "industry first-mover advantage" and its dual technology approach.

CEO Alan Baratz said the results show "strong execution, expanding commercial adoption, and differentiated technology leadership."

data.title: Regeneron Stock (REGN) Buckling as Shareholders Sue Over Cancer Drug Claims
data.description:
A class action lawsuit was filed against biotechnology company Regeneron (REGN) on July 16, which could put further pressure on its troubled share price. The plaintiffs in the lawsuit allege that they bought Regeneron stock at artificially inflated prices between August 1, 2025, and May 15, 2026, known as the Class Period. They are now seeking compensation for financial losses incurred upon public revelation of the company's alleged misconduct during that time – in particular its claims about a new skin cancer drug.

What Does REGN Do?

It is a pharmaceutical company that discovers, invents, develops, manufactures, tests, and commercializes medicines to treat various disorders worldwide. During the relevant period, Regeneron was testing fianlimab, a human monoclonal antibody targeting the LAG-3 immune checkpoint receptor on T-cells, in combination with Libtayo as a first-line treatment for advanced melanoma.

Why are Shareholders Suing REGN?

The complaint alleges that the company made materially false and misleading statements about Regeneron's Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo Study. According to plaintiffs, defendants repeatedly expressed confidence in the drug combination's potential and mischaracterized the risk created by a prolonged slowdown in progression-free survival event accrual.

The complaint alleges defendants did not disclose that the delay could require a protocol change or increase the risk of a negative study outcome.

Regeneron disclosed on May 15, 2026 that the trial had missed its primary endpoint. REGN fell about 9.8% on May 18, 2026, after an earlier 6.2% decline on April 29, 2026.

Its stock is up 5% over the last six months, a slowdown from the 38% growth it has recorded over the last 12 months.

data.title: Is AMD Stock a Sell as Top Executives Quietly Offload Shares and Take Profits
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), a U.S.-based semiconductor giant, is drawing attention after senior executives sold millions of dollars worth of shares this week. The sales came as insiders took profits after the stock's strong gains this year and ahead of the firm's earnings period, when executives faced trading restrictions. Meanwhile, Cathie Wood's investment firm, ARK Invest, has also sold off a considerable portion of its AMD holdings.

AMD Executives Sell Millions of Dollars in Shares

AMD CEO and Chair Lisa Su sold 15,000 shares for about $7.21 million on August 18. According to the firm's SEC filing, she still controlled about 3.85 million AMD shares after the transaction, including both direct and indirect holdings.

On the same day, Ava Hahn, AMD's senior vice president, general counsel, and corporate secretary, sold 2,993 shares for about $1.46 million. The filing showed that she directly held 26,623 AMD shares after the sale.

The sales came after AMD's quarterly earnings blackout period, which prevents executives from illegally trading shares shortly before and after financial results are released. SEC filings show that both Su and Hahn's trades were planned in advance through Rule 10b5-1 trading plans.

The latest move adds to a broader pattern of insider selling at AMD. Chief Technology Officer Mark Papermaster and Chief Strategy Officer Paul Grasby have also reported share sales in recent months. 

Meanwhile, AMD shares closed Thursday at $469.46, up 0.65% according to TipRanks data. The stock extended gains in Friday's premarket trading, moving above $474. Despite the selling, the stock is still up more than 138% over the past six months.

data.title: Why Nvidia Stock Is Trending Higher in Pre-Market Today Ahead of August 26 Earnings
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock is rising in Friday's pre-market trading as investors look ahead to the company's August 26 earnings report. The move comes after a report said Nvidia is in early talks with South Korean AI chipmaker Rebellions about a possible deal. The discussions add another AI-related catalyst for Nvidia just days before its results.

Also, in a new report today, BMO Capital analyst Harsh Kumar initiated coverage of Nvidia with an Outperform rating and a $340 price target, indicating 57% upside from current levels. Kumar, who ranks #9 among the thousands of Wall Street analysts, expects Nvidia to benefit from strong AI demand, saying "much of NVDA's capacity" is sold out for the next 12-plus months.

Nvidia Explores Rebellions Deal as AI Chip Competition Grows

Nvidia is discussing a possible partnership with Rebellions, according to Bloomberg. The talks could also include an investment or an acquisition, although no deal has been agreed.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly met Rebellions CEO Sunghyun Park this week at Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara. Rebellions designs AI chips for data centers and focuses on inference, where AI models process new information.

Rebellions has raised about $850 million from investors, including SK Hynix (SKHY), Samsung Electronics (SSNLF), and Arm Holdings (ARM). The company was last valued at about $2.3 billion.

The talks could give Nvidia another way to expand its AI chip portfolio. They also come after Nvidia's licensing deal with Groq last year, which gave the company access to inference technology.

Nvidia Faces a High Bar on August 26

The bigger near-term event for NVDA stock is its fiscal Q2 report on August 26. Nvidia has guided for $91 billion in revenue, while analysts now expect about $92 billion. Wall Street expects Nvidia to post $2.09 in EPS, nearly double the $1.05 reported a year earlier. Revenue is expected to rise about 95% year over year.
